WorkDaddy

**语言：** [简体中文](README.md) · [English](README_en.md) · [日本語](README_ja.md) > **WorkDaddy 是 WorkBuddy 和 CodeBuddy 桌面端增强助手：多账号独立备份、点切即用，跨账号会话迁移、模型管理与自动化任务。WorkBuddy 还支持免打扰、异常中断自动续接、暂存/快捷提示词和五种主题。账号与配置全部留在本机。** > 本机回环 CDP 注入 · 不改官方安装包。 一个基于 **Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP)** 的 [WorkBuddy](https://www.workbuddy.cn/)、[WorkBuddy AI](https://www.workbuddy.ai/)、[CodeBuddy CN](https://www.codebuddy.cn/) 和 [CodeBuddy](https://www.codebuddy.ai/) 桌面端增强工具。 CodeBuddy 支持范围为 **Electron 智能体窗口**，不包含 VS Code 编辑器模式的增强面板。通过本机调试接口连接运行中的客户端，不修改官方安装包或签名。 ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blueviolet) ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-macOS%2011%2B%20%7C%20Windows%2010%2F11%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey) ![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A522.13-green) --- ## 💖 赞助商 > 想出现在这里？欢迎[联系我们](mailto:richdaddycashmany@163.com)。
Nagora 是专为开发者和团队打造的多模型 AI API 网关。通过一个账户和一枚 API Key，即可统一调用 26+ 款主流文本与图像模型，兼容 OpenAI、Anthropic 与 Gemini 协议，并可无缝接入 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI 等开发工具。平台提供智能路由、自动故障转移、透明计费与统一账单，同时支持预算、限速、并发控制，让个人开发、团队协作和生产环境中的 AI 调用更稳定、更可控。无需改造现有应用，只需替换 Base URL 与 API Key，最快 1 分钟即可完成接入。
--- #### 它能做什么 - **方便切换账号**：每个客户端的账号独立备份，点一下就切，再也不用每次扫码。 - **无感登录新账号**：「登录新账号」支持免退出 OAuth 授权——不退出 WorkBuddy，在浏览器完成扫码后新账号自动加入列表；也可选传统的「假退出」方式回登录页扫码。 - **账号导入导出**：把全部账号备份加密导出，在另一台电脑安装 WorkDaddy 后一键导入，方便电脑之间迁移账号。 - **成长计划与活跃状态**：国内版账号页查询成长任务进度、当日签到和活跃状态、连续活跃天数，以及 Buddy 解锁和旅行状态。 - **Token 和积分用量统计页面**：按天查看 Token 与积分消耗，支持按账号筛选，并显示模型和账号用量排行。 - **积分不足时的账号切换建议**：当前账号积分不足时提示可用账号，方便继续工作。 - **模型频率限制与预计解封时间**：检测到模型限流后，在账号页展示受限模型及预计解封时间。 - **自动化任务**：从 GitHub / Gitee 公开仓库发现并导入任务，或用自然语言让 WorkBuddy 创建任务；支持编辑、手动、事件和定时触发，以及运行日志、停止任务和 JSON / ZIP 导出。 - **权限弹窗免打扰**：真正的零决策弹窗弹出，可以放心开启任务后睡觉。 - **暂存提示词**：输入框边上一键把草稿「暂存」到待发送队列——图片 / 文件 / 引用原样保留，择机发送。 - **切换精美主题**：WorkBuddy 的「接管主题」提供跟随系统、浅色、深色、护眼绿、赛博紫、毛玻璃六种外观；「跟随系统」监听操作系统的深浅色模式变化自动切换，毛玻璃支持预设壁纸、自定义图片壁纸和视频壁纸（MP4 / WebM，静音循环、窗口切后台自动暂停），关闭接管后恢复客户端原生主题。 - **账号间会话迁移**：自动或手动跨账号复制会话，跨账号继续接龙。 - **会话分支**：在「增强」页开启后，任意一条回复都能从此处开始新会话——复制到该条回复为止的聊天内容，原会话保持不变，可在当前工作区继续聊。 - **模型切换更便捷**：解决 WorkBuddy 不支持添加多个同名模型的问题。 - **防止电脑休眠**：睡前任务未完成，开启休眠模式，任务结束后自动切换成允许休眠。 - **异常中断会话自动继续**：AI 回复因网络波动、超时等原因中断时，自动让异常中断任务继续执行。 - **快捷短语**：常用语存进面板，输入框操作栏一键点发； --- ## 客户端与功能范围 | 官方客户端 | 对应安装包品牌 | profile | | -------------------------- | ------------ | ---------------- | | WorkBuddy 国内版 | WorkDaddy | workbuddy-cn | | WorkBuddy AI 国际版 | WorkDaddy AI | `workbuddy-ai` | | CodeBuddy CN 国内版（Electron） | CodeDaddy CN | `codebuddy-cn` | | CodeBuddy 国际版（Electron） | CodeDaddy | `codebuddy-intl` | - 请注意：CodeBuddy 不展示「增强」页；「主题」页仅提供悬浮机器人设置。 ## 演示 ![用量统计图](docs/images/usage.png) ![界面预览图](docs/images/pannel-enhance.png) ![界面预览图](docs/images/pannel-robot.png) ![界面预览图](docs/images/pannel-theme.png) --- ## 安装 先安装并登录上表对应的官方客户端，再下载匹配的增强工具。四款包独立安装、使用各自的账号备份目录；安装包名称中的空格使用连字符。 ### macOS 1. 在 [Releases](../../releases) 下载对应的 `WorkDaddy-x.y.z.dmg`、`WorkDaddy-AI-x.y.z.dmg`、`CodeDaddy-CN-x.y.z.dmg` 或 `CodeDaddy-x.y.z.dmg` 2. 打开 DMG，把里面对应的 `.app` 拖进 **应用程序** 文件夹 3. 第一次打开如果遇到「无法打开，因为 Apple 无法检查恶意软件」： 1. 打开「系统设置 → 隐私与安全性」 2. 在「WorkDaddy 已被阻止」处点 **仍要打开** 3. 输入开机密码确认 ![安装引导](docs/images/install-guide.png) 4. 双击对应的 WorkDaddy / CodeDaddy 应用：它会启动本地守护进程，并把面板注入匹配的客户端。macOS 启动器使用本机 Node.js，建议安装 Node.js 22.13 或更新版本。 5. 看到机器人按钮？**搞定**。 #### 企业专享版 / VPC 客户端 macOS 会自动扫描带 `WorkBuddy` 前缀且包含 `Contents/MacOS/Electron` 的客户端（例如 `WorkBuddy企业定制版.app`），并按 WorkDaddy/WorkDaddy AI profile 排除另一端。发现多个候选时会弹出系统选择窗口，选中后自动记住，不需要手动寻找配置文件。完全自定义名称也可以在源码目录执行下面的高级配置命令： ```bash node scripts/workbuddy-target.js --configure --platform darwin \ --profile workbuddy-cn \ --binary "/Applications/企业客户端.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron" \ --data-dir "$HOME/Library/Application Support/WorkDaddy" ``` ### 会话工作目录恢复 默认不会自动重建已删除的会话工作目录。旧会话需要原目录时，请手动恢复目录；如需启用 Windows 上的自动恢复，可在启动 WorkDaddy 前设置环境变量 `WORKDADDY_REPAIR_MISSING_SESSION_WORKSPACES=1`。启用后，缺失目录会被定期重建。 ### Windows 1. 在 [Releases](../../releases) 下载对应客户端的 `WorkDaddy-Setup-x.y.z.exe`、`WorkDaddy-AI-Setup-x.y.z.exe`、`CodeDaddy-CN-Setup-x.y.z.exe` 或 `CodeDaddy-Setup-x.y.z.exe` 2. 双击安装器完成安装 3. 双击打开对应品牌的桌面快捷方式 #### Windows 便携版 ZIP 不想安装时，可以使用对应的 `<品牌>-Portable-x.y.z.zip`：品牌为 `WorkDaddy`、`WorkDaddy-AI`、`CodeDaddy-CN` 或 `CodeDaddy`。 1. 先安装并登录对应的 WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy 客户端。 2. 将 ZIP 解压到一个有写入权限的目录，不要直接在压缩包内运行。 3. 双击解压目录顶层的 `Start-WorkDaddy.cmd`；也可以直接运行 `WorkDaddyLauncher.exe`。 4. 需要停止后台服务时，运行同目录的 `Stop-WorkDaddy.cmd`。 便携包不会创建桌面快捷方式或卸载项；账号备份和运行数据仍保存在当前用户的 `%APPDATA%\WorkDaddy`，不会随 ZIP 搬走。同一客户端 profile 不能同时运行安装版与便携版，也不能同时运行两份便携版。便携版不使用面板中的自动更新，升级时先运行 `Stop-WorkDaddy.cmd`，确认旧进程停止后再解压新版 ZIP。需要常驻安装和桌面快捷方式时，请下载对应的 Setup.exe。 #### 企业专享版 / VPC 客户端 企业专享版用户仍安装与界面最接近的 `WorkDaddy` 或 `WorkDaddy AI`。安装程序会先自动识别对应的官方客户端，并在安装向导中显示路径和版本；企业版用户点击「浏览」改选自己的 `.exe` 主程序即可，不需要修改配置文件或设置系统环境变量。 选择结果保存在 WorkDaddy 的个人数据目录中。更新安装默认保留上次选择，也可以在安装向导中修改；需要改回官方客户端时，重新运行安装程序并选择自动识别出的官方 `.exe`。WorkDaddy 会锁定所选客户端版本，客户端升级或移动后同样通过安装程序重新确认。 ### Linux Linux 发布包面向 Ubuntu / Debian `amd64` 和 `arm64`，内置对应架构的 Node.js。请先安装并登录同架构的官方客户端；增强工具通过本机调试接口连接，不修改客户端本体。 | 品牌 | DEB 文件 | 安装目录 / Debian 包名 | | ------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | | WorkDaddy | `WorkDaddy_x.y.z_.deb` | `/opt/workdaddy` / `workdaddy` | | WorkDaddy AI | `WorkDaddy-AI_x.y.z_.deb` | `/opt/workdaddy-ai` / `workdaddy-ai` | | CodeDaddy CN | `CodeDaddy-CN_x.y.z_.deb` | `/opt/codedaddy-cn` / `codedaddy-cn` | | CodeDaddy | `CodeDaddy_x.y.z_.deb` | `/opt/codedaddy` / `codedaddy` | 1. 从 [Releases](../../releases) 下载对应文件，`` 为 `amd64` 或 `arm64`。 2. 在下载目录安装选中的包，例如： ```bash sudo apt install ./CodeDaddy-CN_1.2.9_amd64.deb ``` 3. 从应用菜单启动对应品牌的应用。首次启动会准备数据目录并启动后台服务；随后按提示开启客户端 CDP。CodeBuddy 请进入 Electron 智能体窗口。 四款包可以同时安装，互不覆盖，默认不设置开机自启。没有应用菜单时，可运行对应入口： ```bash bash /opt/workdaddy/scripts/launch-gui-linux.sh cn bash /opt/workdaddy-ai/scripts/launch-gui-linux.sh ai bash /opt/codedaddy-cn/scripts/launch-gui-linux.sh codebuddy-cn bash /opt/codedaddy/scripts/launch-gui-linux.sh codebuddy-intl ``` 需要开机启动后台服务时，按对应 profile 启用 systemd 用户服务，例如： ```bash WBSWITCH_PROFILE=codebuddy-cn bash /opt/codedaddy-cn/scripts/systemd-install-linux.sh ``` 用 `sudo apt remove <包名>` 卸载。卸载不会删除账号备份和运行数据；需要清理时，先确认 `~/.config/WorkDaddy` 中对应 profile 的数据。Linux 暂不支持面板内自动更新，请安装新版 DEB 升级。 #### 从源码安装 Linux 版本 在 Linux 主机上执行： ```bash git clone https://github.com/babygoton/WorkDaddy.git cd WorkDaddy bash scripts/install-linux.sh bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp-linux.sh ``` 国际版 WorkBuddy AI 使用隔离环境时执行： ```bash WBSWITCH_PROFILE=workbuddy-ai bash scripts/workbuddy-ai-linux.sh install bash scripts/workbuddy-ai-linux.sh relaunch ``` 需要指定 WorkBuddy 可执行文件时，追加 `WBSWITCH_WORKBUDDY_BIN=/path/to/workbuddy`；安装脚本会创建备份目录、记录客户端路径并启动本地守护进程。 ### 从源码运行（开发者） ```bash git clone https://github.com/babygoton/WorkDaddy.git cd WorkDaddy bash scripts/install.sh # 创建备份目录 + 启动守护进程 bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp.sh # 把 WorkBuddy 切换到调试模式（端口 9222） ``` 四款客户端使用同一套 daemon，通过 profile 绑定客户端，不靠“第一个 CDP 端口”猜测目标： ```bash WBSWITCH_PROFILE=workbuddy-cn bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp.sh WBSWITCH_PROFILE=workbuddy-ai bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp.sh WBSWITCH_PROFILE=codebuddy-cn bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp.sh WBSWITCH_PROFILE=codebuddy-intl bash scripts/relaunch-with-cdp.sh ``` macOS 发布四款 DMG；Linux 为四款客户端分别提供 `amd64`、`arm64` DEB；Windows 构建脚本为四款客户端生成 Setup.exe 和 Portable ZIP。具体可下载的平台与版本以 [Releases](../../releases) 中的资产为准。 ```bash WORKDADDY_BUILD_VERSION=1.2.9 bash scripts/build-mac-dmg.sh WORKDADDY_BUILD_VERSION=1.2.9 WORKDADDY_BUILD_ARCH=amd64 bash scripts/build-linux-deb.sh WORKDADDY_BUILD_VERSION=1.2.9 WORKDADDY_BUILD_ARCH=arm64 bash scripts/build-linux-deb.sh ``` macOS 可用 `WORKDADDY_BUILD_PROFILE` 指定上表中的单个 profile。Windows Portable ZIP 可直接使用；`*-win64.zip` 仅为安装器构建的临时输入，不作为发布包。 `install.sh` 做了： - 创建 `~/Library/Application Support/WorkDaddy` 备份目录 - 首次启动自动兼容迁移旧版 `~/Library/Application Support/HelloBuddy/accounts` 账号备份（旧目录保留不删除） - 首次备份当前 WorkBuddy 账号 - 清理旧 launchd 注册并手动启动守护进程（不再登录自启） - 立即启动后台守护进程 - 打开管理界面 `http://127.0.0.1:47832` > 守护进程会在安装结束时手动启动；需要使用时手动启动对应的 WorkDaddy 端即可。 --- ## 原理 **CDP 注入 · 不改官方安装包** ``` ┌─────────────┐ --remote-debugging-port=9222 ┌──────────────┐ │ WorkBuddy │ <───────────────────────────> │ WorkDaddy │ │ (Electron) │ Chrome DevTools │ daemon.js │ │ │ Protocol (CDP) │ │ │ 渲染进程 │ ←── Runtime.evaluate ──── │ HTTP :47832 │ │ 右下角 │ 注入 inject.js │ 本地 API │ └─────────────┘ └──────────────┘ ``` 以下示意图以 WorkBuddy 国内版为例；四个 profile 的默认本地 API 端口依次为 `47832`、`47833`、`47834`、`47835`，渲染器 CDP 端口依次为 `9222`、`9223`、`9224`、`9225`。CodeBuddy 另用本机主进程调试端口 `9244` / `9245` 访问原生登录态与会话存储。 1. **不修改 WorkBuddy 二进制**：用 `launcher` 启动 WorkBuddy 时多带一个 `--remote-debugging-port=9222` 参数，**二进制与签名原封不动**。 2. **守护进程通过 CDP 连接 WorkBuddy**：监听登录/认证网络事件 + 文件监听兜底，每次登录/刷新令牌都把当前登录信息按 `account.uid` 备份到稳定目录。 3. **注入界面组件**：`Runtime.evaluate` 把 `inject.js` 推到渲染进程执行，在右下角渲染机器人按钮和多标签页面板（账号 / 主题 / 会话 / 模型 / 增强 / 自动化 / 电脑 / 关于 / 设置），按客户端能力显示，CodeBuddy 隐藏「增强」。 4. **本地 HTTP API**：daemon 在 `127.0.0.1:47832` 起服务，组件通过 fetch 调用（账号切换、主题应用、成长进度查询、决策弹窗开关、休眠控制等）。 5. **数据边界清晰**：账号备份和本地配置保存在本机；按功能访问 WorkBuddy 官方 API 或 CodeBuddy 官方 API（登录、积分）和 GitHub Releases（更新检查），显式执行模型连通测试时会向你配置的模型服务发送请求及对应 API Key；脱敏错误诊断默认开启，可在「关于」页关闭。 > 为什么用 CDP 而不是官方插件机制：直接面向运行中的应用实例，事件级感知登录变化， > 主动注入界面与样式补丁，**官方升级 WorkBuddy 后只要界面没大改就照常工作**。 --- ## 使用 ### 面板 WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy Electron 窗口右下角的机器人按钮 → 弹出面板 → 选你要的操作： | Tab | 能做什么 | | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **账号** | 查看账号数、积分、模型频率限制与预计解封时间、当日签到状态、连续活跃天数、成长任务进度及 Buddy 旅行状态；切换、删除或登录新账号，并加密导入导出账号备份 | | **主题** | WorkBuddy：接管主题并选择六种外观（含跟随系统），管理壁纸、头像和背景；CodeBuddy：黑白悬浮机器人设置 | | **会话** | 按账号和时间筛选会话，批量复制或删除，并设置会话 / 工作空间在切换账号时自动复制 | | **模型** | 管理当前模型和备选模型，支持备份、复制、编辑、启用、连通测试及批量删除 | | **增强** | 配置权限免打扰、异常中断自动续接、会话分支、暂存提示词和快捷短语 | | **自动化** | 从 GitHub / Gitee 发现并导入任务、让 WorkBuddy 创建任务，管理触发方式与运行日志，以及 JSON / ZIP 导出 | | **电脑** | 允许或持续禁止休眠，也可在所有 AI 任务结束后自动恢复休眠 | | **关于** | 查看版本和项目说明、检查并安装更新、控制脱敏错误诊断 | | **设置** | 选择中文或英语；首次打开按系统语言匹配，未匹配时使用英语 | **输入框插件（仅 WorkBuddy / WorkBuddy AI）**：在「增强」页分别开启「暂存提示词」和「快捷短语」后，输入框操作栏会显示对应按钮。 暂存提示词可把当前草稿（文字、图片、文件、引用等**完整原样**）加入 WorkBuddy 自带的待发送队列，并暂停自动发送； 入队后输入框自动清空，内容按会话独立保存，可随时发送、编辑或删除。快捷短语可在增强页新增、编辑和批量管理，并从输入框操作栏一键发送，发送后不会自动删除。 ### 自动化 把重复操作保存成任务，例如查询账号积分、按条件显示提醒，或在指定会话发送消息并等待回复。 1. 打开「自动化」页，通过「发现任务」浏览公开仓库中的任务，或使用「让 WorkBuddy 帮我创建」描述需求。WorkBuddy 会在新会话中生成任务，完成后自动加入列表；「查看接口说明」提供当前支持的操作说明。 2. 设置触发方式：手动运行，或在客户端加载、打开面板、页面就绪、账号切换等事件发生时执行；也支持按间隔、每日、每周、每月或指定时间调度。 3. 在列表中启用、停用、编辑或复制任务。手动任务可立即运行，事件和定时任务按配置触发；执行过程中可停止，并通过「运行日志」查看结果和失败步骤。 **任务导入导出**：通过「发现任务」从 GitHub / Gitee 公开仓库导入，导入后保持停用，不覆盖相同 ID 的已有任务；不兼容任务会提示原因。通过批量操作选择任务导出，单个保存为 JSON，多个保存为 ZIP。 #### 提交公开任务 name: polars
description: Extremely fast Query Engine for DataFrames, written in Rust
readme_content:
Documentation: Python - Rust - Node.js - R - SQL | Agents: Skill - MCP | User guide | Discord

## Polars: Extremely fast Query Engine for DataFrames and SQL Polars is an analytical query engine written in Rust. Write your queries with the DataFrame API, in SQL, or mix both: they run through the same optimizer and the same engine. It is designed to be fast, easy to use and expressive. Key features are: - **Fast**: written from the ground up in Rust with multi-threaded, vectorized (SIMD) execution - **Spill to disk**: Operations that exceed available RAM can spill to disk - **Expressive API**: compose complex queries with powerful expressions - **Extensible**: extend Polars natively with custom code through [I/O and Expression plugins](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/plugins/) - **GPU support**: optionally accelerate queries on NVIDIA GPUs - **Interoperable**: uses the [Apache Arrow Columnar Format](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Columnar.html) for zero-copy data sharing To learn more, read the [user guide](https://docs.pola.rs/). ## Polars in action ### DataFrame API Queries are composed from expressions or SQL. This lazy query gets optimized out of the box and runs in parallel across all available cores: ```python import polars as pl df = ( pl.scan_parquet("orders.parquet") .filter(pl.col("status") == "shipped") .group_by("customer_id") .agg( pl.col("amount").sum().alias("total"), pl.len().alias("n_orders"), ) .sort("total", descending=True) .collect() ) ``` ### SQL ```python import polars as pl df = pl.sql(""" WITH totals AS ( SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n_orders FROM read_parquet('orders.parquet') WHERE status = 'shipped' GROUP BY customer_id ) SELECT c.name, t.total, t.n_orders, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY t.total DESC) AS rank FROM totals t JOIN read_parquet('customers.parquet') c USING (customer_id) ORDER BY t.total DESC """).collect() ``` ### Mix both DataFrames and LazyFrames in scope can be queried by name, and the result of a SQL query is a regular `LazyFrame`, so you can switch between SQL and expressions freely: ```python orders = pl.scan_parquet("orders.parquet") df = ( pl.sql("SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id") .filter(pl.col("total") > 1_000) .collect() ) ``` Read more in the [SQL user guide](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/sql/intro/). ## Performance Polars is very fast. In fact, it is one of the best performing query engines available, for both DataFrame and SQL workloads. See the [PDS-H benchmarks](https://www.pola.rs/benchmarks.html) results. ## Installation ### Python Install the latest Polars version with: ```sh pip install polars ``` See the [User Guide](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/installation/#feature-flags) for more details on optional dependencies
Compile Polars from source If you want a bleeding edge release you should compile Polars from source. Advanced users can also compile for maximum performance for their architecture. This can be done by going through the following steps in sequence: 1. Install the latest [Rust compiler](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install) 2. Install [maturin](https://maturin.rs/): `pip install maturin` 3. `cd py-polars` and choose one of the following: - `make build`, slow binary with debug assertions and limited symbols, fast compile times - `make build-debug`, same as `make build`, but with all symbols, produces large binaries - `make build-release`, fast binary without debug assertions, minimal debug symbols, long compile times - `make build-nodebug-release`, same as build-release but without any debug symbols, slightly faster to compile - `make build-debug-release`, same as build-release but with full debug symbols, slightly slower to compile - `make build-dist-release`, fastest binary, extreme compile times By default the binary is compiled with optimizations turned on for a modern CPU. Specify `LTS_CPU=1` with the command if your CPU is older and does not support e.g. AVX2. Note that the Rust crate implementing the Python bindings is called `py-polars` to distinguish from the wrapped Rust crate `polars` itself. However, both the Python package and the Python module are named `polars`, so you can `pip install polars` and `import polars`.
Check the [Installation guide](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/installation/) for more advanced installations. For example when you expect more than 2^32 (~4.2 billion) rows, run on an old CPU (e.g. dating from before 2011), or on an `x86-64` build of Python on Apple Silicon under Rosetta. ## Contributing Want to contribute? Read our [contributing guide](https://docs.pola.rs/development/contributing/) and check the issue tracker for accepted issues. Contributors new to the codebase can look for the `good first issue` label to get familiar with the project. You can [join the Polars Discord server](https://discord.gg/4UfP5cfBE7) for any help along the way. ## Distributed Polars Running into hardware limitations executing your queries? Read how you can [horizontally scale your Polars query on a cluster](https://docs.nanook.pola.rs/). ## License Polars is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE) (SPDX: `MIT`).

name: mastra
description: Mastra is the modern TypeScript framework for AI-powered applications and agents.
readme_content:
# Mastra [![npm version](https://badge.fury.io/js/@mastra%2Fcore.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mastra/core) [![CodeQl](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/actions/workflows/github-code-scanning/codeql/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/actions/workflows/github-code-scanning/codeql) [![GitHub Repo stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/mastra-ai/mastra)](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/stargazers) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1309558646228779139?logo=discord&label=Discord&labelColor=white&color=7289DA)](https://discord.gg/mastra-ai) [![Twitter Follow](https://img.shields.io/twitter/follow/mastra?style=social)](https://x.com/mastra) [![NPM Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/%40mastra%252Fcore)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mastra/core) [![Static Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/Y%20Combinator-W25-orange)](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies?batch=W25) Mastra is a framework for building AI-powered applications and agents with a modern TypeScript stack. It includes everything you need to go from early prototypes to production-ready applications. Mastra integrates with frontend and backend frameworks like React, Next.js, and Node, or you can deploy it anywhere as a standalone server. It's the easiest way to build, tune, and scale reliable AI products. ## Why Mastra? Purpose-built for TypeScript and designed around established AI patterns, Mastra gives you everything you need to build great AI applications out-of-the-box. Some highlights include: - [**Model routing**](https://mastra.ai/models): Connect to 40+ providers through one standard interface. Use models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and more. - [**Agents**](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/overview): Build autonomous agents that use LLMs and tools to solve open-ended tasks. Agents reason about goals, decide which tools to use, and iterate internally until the model emits a final answer or an optional stopping condition is met. - [**Workflows**](https://mastra.ai/docs/workflows/overview): When you need explicit control over execution, use Mastra's graph-based workflow engine to orchestrate complex multi-step processes. Mastra workflows use an intuitive syntax for control flow (`.then()`, `.branch()`, `.parallel()`). - [**Human-in-the-loop**](https://mastra.ai/docs/workflows/suspend-and-resume): Suspend an agent or workflow and await user input or approval before resuming. Mastra uses [storage](https://mastra.ai/docs/server-db/storage) to remember execution state, so you can pause indefinitely and resume where you left off. - **Context management**: Give your agents the right context at the right time. Provide [conversation history](https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/conversation-history), [retrieve](https://mastra.ai/docs/rag/overview) data from your sources (APIs, databases, files), and add human-like memory with [Observational Memory](https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/observational-memory) so your agents behave coherently. - **Integrations**: Bundle agents and workflows into existing React, Next.js, or Node.js apps, or ship them as standalone endpoints. When building UIs, integrate with agentic libraries like Vercel's AI SDK UI and CopilotKit to bring your AI assistant to life on the web. - [**MCP servers**](https://mastra.ai/docs/tools-mcp/mcp-overview): Author Model Context Protocol servers, exposing agents, tools, and other structured resources via the MCP interface. These can then be accessed by any system or agent that supports the protocol. - **Production essentials**: Shipping reliable agents takes ongoing insight, evaluation, and iteration. With built-in [evals](https://mastra.ai/docs/evals/overview) and [observability](https://mastra.ai/docs/observability/overview), Mastra gives you the tools to observe, measure, and refine continuously. ## Get started The **recommended** way to get started with Mastra is by running the command below: ```shell npm create mastra@latest ``` Follow the [Installation guide](https://mastra.ai/docs) for step-by-step setup with the CLI or a manual install. If you're new to AI agents, check out our [templates](https://mastra.ai/docs/getting-started/templates), [course](https://mastra.ai/course), and [YouTube videos](https://youtube.com/@mastra-ai) to start building with Mastra today.
Alternative: Use this pre-built prompt to get started ```md Create a new Mastra project. Mastra is a framework for AI applications and agents on a modern TypeScript stack. Before running the command, ask these questions one at a time and wait for each answer unless it was already provided: 1. Project name? (default: "my-mastra-app") 2. Provider? (required; options: "openai", "anthropic", "google", "xai") If the provider isn't supported, ask again and list the supported values. Run: `npm create mastra@latest -- --llm ` The command creates a default Mastra project, installs Mastra skills for detected coding assistants, and initializes Git when appropriate. After creation, enter the project directory and start the dev server: `npx bgproc start -n -w -- npm run dev` Open Mastra Studio at `http://localhost:4111`. Studio is the interface for building, testing, and managing agents, workflows, and tools. Also mention that the Mastra model router provides access to thousands of models: https://mastra.ai/models ```
## Documentation Visit our [official documentation](https://mastra.ai/docs). ## Build with AI Learn how to make your agent a Mastra expert by following the [Build with AI guide](https://mastra.ai/reference/build-with-ai). ## Contributing Looking to contribute? Pull requests are limited to collaborators only. Therefore you can _best_ help by creating high-quality issues with good reproductions and descriptions. Mastra will then verify your report and prioritize it accordingly. If you want to run Mastra or its tests locally, refer to the [development documentation](./DEVELOPMENT.md) ## Support We have an [open community Discord](https://discord.gg/mastra-ai). Come and say hello and let us know if you have any questions or need any help getting things running. It's also super helpful if you leave the project a star here, at the [top of the page](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra) ## Licensing This repository uses a dual-license model: - **Apache License 2.0**: The core framework and the vast majority of this codebase is open source under Apache-2.0. - **Mastra Enterprise License**: Code in any directory named `ee/` (e.g., `packages/core/src/auth/ee/`) is source-available under the Mastra Enterprise License. These features require a valid enterprise license for production use but can be freely used for development and testing. See [LICENSE.md](./LICENSE.md) for the full license mapping and [ee/LICENSE](./ee/LICENSE) for the enterprise license terms. ## Security We are committed to maintaining the security of this repo and of Mastra as a whole. If you discover a security finding we ask you to please responsibly disclose this to us at [security@mastra.ai](mailto:security@mastra.ai) and we will get back to you.

name: pgrust
description: Postgres rewritten in Rust, now faster than Postgres and Clickhouse
readme_content:
pgrust

A Postgres-compatible database, rewritten in Rust, built for fast analytics on your Postgres data.

Try pgrust in your browser →   |   Discord   |   Updates   |   Issues

> **New:** [Video of Michael's talk at PlanetScale on pgrust](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7L_nG3EBjck) — and the [slides](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_wDk4HPE9-MuiPBo_X-QdJUmFtVV0p8p/view). > > [How AI Changes the Economics of JIT Compilers](https://malisper.me/how-ai-changes-the-economics-of-jit-compilers/) > > **v0.4-beta is out:** [the release post](https://pgrust.com/blog/pgrust-v0-4-beta/) and [what's new](#whats-new-in-v04-beta). pgrust is a drop-in replacement for Postgres built for fast analytics. It is wire compatible and SQL dialect compatible with Postgres 18, so your existing drivers, ORMs, `psql` and tools work unchanged. It is Postgres rebuilt the way it would be built in 2026. Every line is Rust, written to match the behavior of the C implementation. Rust makes it easy to re-architect several core Postgres pieces. pgrust has: - Gravity, a new vectorized push-based, JIT compiled query engine - A thread based concurrency model - A query scheduler designed to keep any individual query from taking down your database - An automatic memory manager: one memory budget, sized from the machine, covers the buffer pool, the columnar caches and running queries, and gives pgrust control of what happens when you're running low on memory, greatly reducing the chance of your whole DB being taken down by the OS OOM killer and many other really awesome pieces. The scheduler and the memory manager go after two of [the four horsemen behind thousands of Postgres outages](https://malisper.me/the-four-horsemen-behind-thousands-of-postgres-outages/). ## Quickstart **In your browser:** , a full pgrust server compiled to WebAssembly, no install. **On your machine:** download a release tarball from . Each one is self-contained: it carries pgrust's own `bin/postgres`, `bin/initdb` and `bin/psql` plus the share files they read, so you do not need a PostgreSQL install. The Linux binaries need glibc 2.34 or newer (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL/Rocky 9 and later); the macOS binaries need macOS 11 or newer. | Tarball | Runs on | |---|---| | [`pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-x86_64.tar.gz) | any x86-64 CPU | | [`pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-aarch64.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-aarch64.tar.gz) | any 64-bit Arm CPU | | [`pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-x86_64-znver3.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-x86_64-znver3.tar.gz) | tuned for AMD Zen 3 and newer | | [`pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-aarch64-neoverse-v2.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-aarch64-neoverse-v2.tar.gz) | tuned for Neoverse-V2 (AWS Graviton4, NVIDIA Grace) | | [`pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-arm64.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-arm64.tar.gz) | macOS on Apple Silicon | | [`pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-x86_64.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-x86_64.tar.gz) | macOS on Intel | | [`pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-universal.tar.gz`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-macos-universal.tar.gz) | macOS, either (both architectures in one binary) | The Linux builds are profile-guided optimized. The tuned builds use instructions only those CPUs (and newer ones) have; when in doubt, take the generic build. Every tarball has a `.sha256` file next to it, and [`MANIFEST.txt`](https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/MANIFEST.txt) lists them all. ### Linux ```bash # Pick your build: linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, linux-x86_64-znver3 or # linux-aarch64-neoverse-v2 (see the table above). PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 # Download pgrust, verify the checksum and unpack it. curl -LO "https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -LO "https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar xzf "pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" cd pgrust-0.4-beta-linux-*/ # Create a data directory with pgrust's initdb. bin/initdb -D /tmp/pgrust-data --no-locale --encoding UTF8 -U postgres # Start the server. It runs in the foreground and logs to this terminal. ulimit -s 65520 RUST_MIN_STACK=33554432 bin/postgres \ -D /tmp/pgrust-data \ -k /tmp -p 5432 \ -c listen_addresses= \ -c io_method=sync \ -c max_stack_depth=60000 ``` Leave the server running and connect from a second terminal, in the same directory: ```bash bin/psql -h /tmp -p 5432 -U postgres -c "select version()" ``` You should see `PostgreSQL 18.6 (pgrust 0.4-beta, build ) on ...`, where `` is the short commit the binary was built from. `bin/postgres --version` prints `pgrust 0.4-beta (PostgreSQL 18.6 compatible)`. ### Docker The prebuilt image on Docker Hub, [`malisper/pgrust`](https://hub.docker.com/r/malisper/pgrust), is a drop-in replacement for the official `postgres` image: same env vars (`POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_DB`, `PGDATA`, ...), same `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` init scripts, same data volume at `/var/lib/postgresql/data`. It carries the same `postgres` and `initdb` binaries as the Linux release tarballs above, and initializes the cluster with pgrust's own `initdb`; the only C PostgreSQL component in the image is `psql` for the init scripts. `malisper/pgrust:v0.4-beta` is multi-arch (amd64 + arm64); `v0.4-beta-amd64` and `v0.4-beta-arm64` pin one architecture. ```bash docker run -d --name pgrust -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret -p 5432:5432 malisper/pgrust:v0.4-beta ``` Then connect, with your own `psql` or the one in the image: ```bash psql -h localhost -p 5432 -U postgres docker exec -it pgrust psql -U postgres ``` `malisper/pgrust:latest` still points at v0.3; use the `v0.4-beta` tag to get this release. A data volume written by v0.3 holding columnar tables needs the dump and restore described under [Stopping, restarting, cleaning up](#stopping-restarting-cleaning-up). ### macOS ```bash # Pick your build: macos-arm64 (Apple Silicon), macos-x86_64 (Intel) or # macos-universal (both). PLATFORM=macos-arm64 # Download pgrust, verify the checksum and unpack it. Download with curl: curl # does not set the quarantine flag a browser download gets, so Gatekeeper stays # out of the way (see the note below). curl -LO "https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -LO "https://pgrust.com/downloads/v0.4-beta/pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" shasum -a 256 -c "pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar xzf "pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" cd "pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM" # Create a data directory with pgrust's initdb. bin/initdb -D /tmp/pgrust-data --no-locale --encoding UTF8 -U postgres # Start the server. It runs in the foreground and logs to this terminal. ulimit -s 65520 RUST_MIN_STACK=33554432 bin/postgres \ -D /tmp/pgrust-data \ -k /tmp -p 5432 \ -c listen_addresses= \ -c io_method=sync \ -c max_stack_depth=60000 ``` Leave the server running and connect from a second terminal, in the same directory: ```bash bin/psql -h /tmp -p 5432 -U postgres -c "select version()" ``` **A note on Gatekeeper:** the macOS binaries are signed ad hoc, not notarized by Apple. Downloaded with curl as above, they are never quarantined and none of this comes up. If you download with a browser instead, macOS refuses to run them with "Apple could not verify ... is free of malware". Clear the flag with `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine pgrust-0.4-beta-$PLATFORM`, or approve each binary under System Settings > Privacy & Security > "Open Anyway". ### Columnar tables Columnar storage (`pgrcolumnar`) is a table access method. Register it once in each database, then create tables with `USING pgrcolumnar`: ```sql CREATE ACCESS METHOD pgrcolumnar TYPE TABLE HANDLER heap_tableam_handler; CREATE TABLE events (id bigint, kind text, val double precision, at timestamp) USING pgrcolumnar; ``` ### Stopping, restarting, cleaning up - **Stop the server** with Ctrl-C in its terminal, or `kill -INT `. That is Postgres' fast shutdown and it is safe. - **Start it again** by rerunning the same server command with the same data directory. Your data is preserved across restarts. - **Start over** by deleting the data directory: `rm -rf /tmp/pgrust-data`. This deletes all data in it. - **If startup fails with** `FATAL: lock file "/tmp/.s.PGSQL.5432.lock" already exists`, another server, most likely an existing Postgres install, is already using port 5432. Start pgrust on a different port with `-p 5433` and connect with `psql -h /tmp -p 5433 -U postgres`. Whenever a regular Postgres is running on the same machine, check `select version()` after connecting; it is easy to silently connect to the wrong server and wonder why nothing behaves like pgrust. - **If startup fails with** `could not open directory "/usr/local/pgsql/share/timezone"`, the server cannot find its share files. It reads them from the `share` directory beside the binary, so run `bin/postgres` from the unpacked tarball as is, without moving the binary away from `bin/share`. `PGRUST_PGSHAREDIR` and `PGRUST_TZDIR` point it elsewhere. - **Columnar tables from v0.3** (`USING pgrcolumnar`) are refused with an error saying the table is in the v0.3.x columnar format. Dump them with the v0.3 binary (`pg_dump`) and restore them into v0.4-beta. ## When to use pgrust - **Analytics on your Postgres data without a separate warehouse.** Put large tables in `pgrcolumnar` and query them with the same SQL, in the same database as your application data. - **Speeding up slow Postgres queries** with large scans, joins and aggregations, such as dashboards and reporting. - **One database for transactions and analytics**, instead of Postgres plus ClickHouse or a warehouse kept in sync by a pipeline. ## Status We're working with a few early design partners and are targeting production readiness in Q1 2027. Testing and reliability are our top priority; see [Testing](#testing) for how we verify pgrust against Postgres. We run pgrust ourselves internally today. ## Extensions pgrust ships the most-used Postgres extensions built in: pgvector, pg_cron, pg_stat_statements, pg_trgm, hstore, pgcrypto, postgres_fdw and most of contrib. Install them with `CREATE EXTENSION` as usual. pgrust doesn't load C extension binaries compiled for Postgres, but porting an existing extension to pgrust is straightforward, and we add new ones regularly. If you need an extension that isn't listed, [open an issue](https://github.com/malisper/pgrust/issues) and we'll prioritize it. PL/Python, PL/Perl and PL/Tcl are not supported yet. ## Performance Measured on `c8g.4xlarge` (AWS Graviton4), pgrust with pgrcolumnar, its builtin columnar layout, runs ClickBench's analytical queries up to 1,600x faster than PostgreSQL (per query, cold runs, against PostgreSQL's published results on the same instance type). For a code-level walkthrough of one part of that speedup, read [how batchi

description: Plugins, agents, skills, and commands for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Pi, written once in Markdown and adapted to each tool by generators with validation and evals.
readme_content: # Plugins, agents, and skills for AI coding tools **New:** A deterministic judge scored the Verified versions of two workflows. [See the scorecards](docs/verified/README.md) or join the [agents Verified waitlist](https://buy.polar.sh/polar_cl_yAj2XSCMpSY3vYTcoymlT102uGuJIAKgAI6134QYG9n). Verified is a paid product from Major7 Apps, founded by this repository’s maintainer. Use one collection of plugins, agents, skills, and commands across Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Pi. A harness is the coding tool that loads and runs the components. Contributors write each component once, in Markdown, in the Claude Code plugin format. Adapters under `tools/adapters/` generate the format each harness reads, map model aliases to that harness's models, and translate tool permissions where the harness supports them. CI regenerates the artifacts for every harness, validates them, and runs the OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, and Pi artifacts through their installed CLIs. The [capability matrix](docs/harnesses.md) lists what each harness supports, and [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) describes the design. The catalog contains 93 plugins, including 91 local plugins and 2 external entries. The local source contains 199 agents, 185 skills, and 103 commands. Plugins cover Python and JavaScript development, code review, testing, infrastructure, security, and other work. ## Multi-harness support Choose the harness you use and follow its setup route. Available components depend on the installation route and the harness's capabilities. | Tool | Installation | Components and limits | |---|---|---| | [Claude Code](#claude-code) | Plugin marketplace | Source agents, skills, and commands; plugin-specific hooks and MCP configuration | | [OpenAI Codex CLI](#codex-cli) | Native marketplace or generated artifacts | Native source skills; generated TOML agents and commands as skills use a separate route | | [Cursor](#cursor) | Plugin marketplace | Source agents, skills, and commands, with curated project rules | | [OpenCode](#install-from-a-clone) | `make install-opencode` | Generated agents, skills, and commands, with translated tool permissions | | [Antigravity CLI](#install-from-a-clone) | `make install-antigravity` | Generated plugins containing agents, skills, and commands | | [GitHub Copilot](#install-from-a-clone) | `make install-copilot` | Generated agent profiles and skills; commands also become invocable skills | | [Pi](#install-from-a-clone) | `make install-pi` | Generated skills and prompt templates; agents require a subagent extension | See the [capability matrix](docs/harnesses.md) for model mappings, tool permissions, hooks, and installation differences. For individual skills, use a [skills-only installer](#skills-only) and select your coding tool. ## How it works A plugin groups related agents, skills, and commands under `plugins/`. For example, `python-development` contains three agents, sixteen skills, and a scaffolding command. The chosen harness loads the installed components according to its own discovery and invocation rules. Contributors maintain one Markdown source in the Claude Code plugin format. Native registries point to that source where supported, and adapters generate the formats needed by each harness. Commands may become skills or prompt templates, and agent formats, model choices, and tool permissions vary by harness. Source agents specify model aliases such as `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`, `fable`, or `inherit`. Adapters map those aliases to each harness's model settings, including fixed defaults for some `inherit` entries. See [model configuration](docs/agents.md#model-configuration) and the [adapter mappings](tools/adapters/capabilities.py). ## Quality evaluation The repository validates plugin structure, generated artifacts, and documentation. Contributors can run these checks from the repository root: ```bash make generate-all make validate STRICT=1 make garden ``` [`plugin-eval`](plugins/plugin-eval/) also provides static skill checks without model calls. For example: ```bash uv run --project plugins/plugin-eval plugin-eval score plugins/python-development/skills/python-testing-patterns --depth quick ``` The LLM judge and Monte Carlo layers are experimental and are not validated against human labels. Their scores describe model assessments and repeated simulations and do not prove that a task succeeds in a project. They require the optional `llm` dependencies. Model calls use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` when it is set and bill that API account. Otherwise they use your Claude Code login. See the [evaluation guide](docs/plugin-eval.md) for setup and limits. ## Verified workflows Some workflows in this repo are being measured. Each one runs on a fixed set of test cases, several times per harness and model, and the results are published with confidence intervals. Runs repeat after each Claude Code release, and other coding tools join as their runs are wired up. - Method and current scores: [docs/verified](docs/verified/README.md) - Join the [waitlist for agents Verified](https://buy.polar.sh/polar_cl_yAj2XSCMpSY3vYTcoymlT102uGuJIAKgAI6134QYG9n), the tuned and re-tested versions. The free catalog stays MIT and keeps getting updates. Verified is a separate, paid layer sold by Major7 Apps, which this repository's maintainer founded. To support the free catalog directly, see [SPONSORING.md](SPONSORING.md). ## Quick start Choose a plugin for the work you do: | Plugin | Use it for | |---|---| | [python-development](plugins/python-development/) | Python, Django, FastAPI, testing, and packaging | | [javascript-typescript](plugins/javascript-typescript/) | JavaScript and TypeScript development and project setup | | [developer-essentials](plugins/developer-essentials/) | Code review, debugging, Git, and testing patterns | | [security-scanning](plugins/security-scanning/) | Security review, dependency checks, and code scanning | See the [plugin catalog](docs/plugins.md) for all 93 plugins and the [usage guide](docs/usage.md) for commands and examples. ### Claude Code Run these commands inside Claude Code to register the marketplace and install the Python development plugin: ```text /plugin marketplace add wshobson/agents /plugin install python-development@claude-code-workflows ``` Then ask Claude to use the Python agents for your task, or run the plugin's scaffolding command: ```text /python-development:python-scaffold Create a FastAPI service with tests ``` ### Codex CLI Run these commands in a terminal with a current Codex CLI: ```bash codex plugin marketplace add wshobson/agents codex plugin add python-development@claude-code-workflows ``` The native Codex manifests expose source skills. The generated TOML agents and command-derived skills use a separate adapter path. Native installation also reads the original skill bodies, while generated copies split oversized bodies into reference files for the 8 KB budget. See the [Codex setup details](docs/harnesses.md#native-install) before choosing an installation route. ### Cursor Cursor uses the committed [plugin marketplace registry](.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json). Follow the [Cursor setup instructions](docs/harnesses.md#native-install) to add the marketplace and install a plugin. ### Skills only Install an individual skill with GitHub CLI's `gh skill` command or the `npx skills` installer. Select your coding tool when prompted. Both installers read skills from GitHub without cloning the repository and install them without the plugin's agents, commands, or hooks. ```bash gh skill install wshobson/agents python-testing-patterns npx skills add wshobson/agents --skill python-testing-patterns ``` `gh skill` requires GitHub CLI 2.90 or later. The `npx` command requires Node.js and npm. See [skills-only installation](docs/harnesses.md#skills-only-installers) for other agents, install scopes, and version pinning. ### Install from a clone For OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Pi, clone the repository and use the installer for your harness. Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), Python 3.12 or later, and the coding tool you want to use. The following clone command uses GitHub CLI: ```bash gh repo clone wshobson/agents ~/agents cd ~/agents ``` Run the command for your tool. Each target generates the artifacts and links all local plugins into that tool's user configuration: ```bash make install-opencode make install-antigravity make install-copilot make install-pi ``` Pi's agents require its reference `subagent` extension or a compatible extension. See the [global install guide](docs/harnesses.md#global-install) for configuration paths and uninstall commands. ## What's inside | Component | Count | Purpose | |---|---:|---| | Plugins | 93 | Installable groups of components, including 91 local plugins and 2 external entries | | Agents | 199 | Instructions for specialist subagents that handle delegated work | | Skills | 185 | Guidance and reference material that an agent loads when relevant | | Commands | 103 | Named workflows you invoke, such as project scaffolding or a security scan | The agent, skill, and command counts cover local source files.
